Title: The Last Kids on Earth and the Zombie Parade
Author: Max Brallier (illustrated by Douglas Holgate)
Subject: Zombies, Monsters, Friendship
Summary: The zombies start vanishing from town, which turns out to be worse news than it sounds. Book two of the series.

Title: The Last Little Cat
Author: Meindert DeJong
Subject: Animals, Perseverance
Summary: The runt of a litter in a dog kennel is turned out into the world and must find his own way to a home, told with quiet tension by a Newbery-winning author.

Title: The Laws Guide to Nature Drawing and Journaling
Author: John Muir Laws
Subject: Nature Journaling, Drawing, Observation
Summary: A thorough guide to keeping a nature journal — drawing technique, observation practice, note-taking and curiosity as a method.

Title: The Lewis & Clark Expedition
Author: Richard L. Neuberger
Subject: Exploration, American West, Landmark Books
Summary: The 1804-1806 journey from St. Louis to the Pacific and back, written for young readers in the Landmark Books series.

Title: The Light of All That Falls
Author: James Islington
Subject: Prophecy, Magic, Time
Summary: The loops close and the cost of the Boundary comes due. Final book of the Licanius Trilogy.

Title: The Little Gnome Tenderroot
Author: Jakob Streit
Subject: Gnomes, Nature, Earth
Summary: A gnome's underground life among roots, stones and crystals, in the nature-story tradition Streit wrote for young Waldorf classes.

Title: The Lost Words: Spell Songs
Author: Folk by the Oak (songs inspired by Robert Macfarlane and Jackie Morris)
Subject: Nature Words, Folk Music, Illustration
Summary: A book-and-CD set of songs written by a folk supergroup in response to Macfarlane and Morris's The Lost Words, with accompanying artwork. Included here as a non-book item, with the format noted.

Title: The Lost World
Author: Michael Crichton
Subject: Dinosaurs, Islands, Genetics
Summary: Six years after Jurassic Park, a second island of engineered dinosaurs draws another expedition. Crichton's sequel.

Title: The Magic Ball of Wool
Author: Susanna Isern (illustrated by Nora Hilb)
Subject: Kindness, Knitting, Sharing
Summary: A boy discovers a ball of wool that never runs out and uses it to knit gifts for everyone who needs one. A picture book about generosity and the quiet good that small acts do.

Title: The Magic Finger
Author: Roald Dahl
Subject: Magic, Hunting, Reversal
Summary: A girl whose anger gives her a magic finger turns it on a family of duck hunters, who wake up with wings.

Title: The Magic Knot & Other Tangles!
Author: Reg Down
Subject: Fairies, Humor, Nature Stories
Summary: A comedy starring the gnomes Pine Cone and Pepper Pot alongside Tiptoes Lightly, full of tangles, mishaps and small woodland magic.

Title: The Magical Unicorn Society Official Coloring Book
Author: Selwyn E. Phipps
Subject: Unicorns, Coloring
Summary: A coloring companion to the Magical Unicorn Society books.

Title: The Magical Worlds of Harry Potter
Author: David Colbert
Subject: Harry Potter, Folklore, Etymology
Summary: Short entries tracing the myths, legends, and word origins behind names and creatures in the Harry Potter books.

Title: The Martian
Author: Andy Weir
Subject: Mars, Survival, Engineering
Summary: An astronaut left behind on Mars keeps himself alive with botany, chemistry, and stubbornness while NASA works out a rescue.

Title: The Middle Ages for Kids: Through the Lives of Kings, Heroes, and Saints
Author: Catherine Fet
Subject: Medieval History, Biography
Summary: Medieval history told the old-fashioned way — as a sequence of short, memorable biographical stories about the era's kings, heroes and saints, richly illustrated with period art.

Title: The Middle Ages: A Graphic History
Author: Eleanor Janega (illustrated by Neil Max Emmanuel)
Subject: Medieval History, Myth-Busting, Comics
Summary: A comics history of medieval Europe that takes aim at the Dark Ages caricature. Introducing Books.

Title: The Midsummer Mouse
Author: Reg Down
Subject: Summer, Fairies, Nature Stories
Summary: Midsummer tales of Tiptoes Lightly and the Summer Queen, following the high-summer doings of the meadow and its small inhabitants.

Title: The Midsummer Tomte and the Little Rabbits
Author: Ulf Stark (illustrated by Eva Eriksson)
Subject: Midsummer, Tomte, Sweden
Summary: Grump the tomte shelters the forest animals after a storm wrecks the rabbit children's Midsummer plans. Told in twenty-one short chapters meant to be read a day at a time through June.

Title: The Mitten
Author: Jan Brett
Subject: Ukrainian Folktale, Winter, Animals
Summary: Nicki loses a white wool mitten in the snow and one animal after another crowds inside it until it can stretch no further. Brett's retelling of a Ukrainian folktale, with her signature bordered illustrations.

Title: The Mitten Thief
Author: Jill Kaufenberg
Subject: Winter, Mystery, Friendship
Summary: Sisters Molly and Jules keep losing their mittens, and a snowy outdoor adventure with their friends reveals what has really been happening to them beneath the snow piles — after which the kids hatch a plan to return every mitten to its owner.

Title: The Moomins and the Great Flood
Author: Tove Jansson
Subject: Moomins, Adventure, Family
Summary: The first Moomin book: Moominmamma and Moomintroll search for Moominpappa through a flooded, strange landscape and find their way to the Moominvalley.

Title: The Moon
Author: Hannah Pang (illustrated by Thomas Hegbrook)
Subject: Moon, Astronomy, Culture
Summary: The moon across science, mythology and human history, from tides and phases to lunar landings and lunar legends.

Title: The Mysteries of the Universe
Author: Will Gater (illustrated by Angela Rizza and Daniel Long)
Subject: Astronomy, Space, Solar System
Summary: A gold-and-navy illustrated guide to more than one hundred objects in space — planets, moons, nebulae, galaxies and black holes — with the science and the stories behind each.

Title: The Name of the Wind
Author: Patrick Rothfuss
Subject: Magic School, Music, Storytelling
Summary: Kvothe, now an innkeeper in hiding, tells the first day of his own story: orphaned, destitute, and clawing his way into the University. Tenth Anniversary Edition.

Title: The New York Times Best of the Week Series: Monday Crosswords
Author: edited by Will Shortz
Subject: Crosswords, Puzzles
Summary: A collection of the week's easiest New York Times crosswords, all Monday puzzles.

Title: The Noisy Paint Box
Author: Barb Rosenstock (illustrated by Mary GrandPré)
Subject: Kandinsky, Synesthesia, Abstract Art
Summary: The story of Vasya Kandinsky, who heard colors as sounds and painted the first abstract art despite everyone telling him to paint what he saw.

Title: The Odyssey
Author: Homer, retold by Gillian Cross (illustrated by Neil Packer)
Subject: Greek Mythology, Epic Poetry
Summary: Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy past the Cyclops, Circe, the Sirens and Scylla, retold for children with striking graphic illustrations.

Title: The Odyssey
Author: Homer (illustrated by Manuela Adreani)
Subject: Greek Mythology, Epic Poetry
Summary: A large-format picture-book edition of Odysseus's journey home, with lush painterly illustrations by Manuela Adreani.

Title: The Odyssey
Author: Homer (translated by Robert Fitzgerald)
Subject: Greek Epic, Odysseus, Translation
Summary: Fitzgerald's verse translation of Odysseus's ten-year voyage home from Troy. A third distinct edition of the Odyssey in this collection, alongside the Gillian Cross and Manuela Adreani versions.

Title: The Once and Future King
Author: T.H. White
Subject: Arthurian Legend, Kingship, War
Summary: White's retelling of Malory, from Arthur's education by Merlyn through the collapse of Camelot. Collected in one volume.

Title: The Once Upon a Time Map Book
Author: B.G. Hennessy (illustrated by Peter Joyce)
Subject: Maps, Fairy Tales
Summary: Six fold-out maps of storybook lands — Oz, Neverland, Wonderland, the Giant's kingdom and more — with directions and treasure-hunt tasks for readers to follow.

Title: The Overstory
Author: Richard Powers
Subject: Trees, Activism, Ecology
Summary: Nine strangers are drawn separately toward the fate of the world's remaining forests. Winner of the Pulitzer Prize.

Title: The Panama Canal
Author: Bob Considine
Subject: Engineering, Panama, Landmark Books
Summary: The building of the canal, from the failed French attempt through the American construction and the fight against yellow fever. A Landmark Book.

Title: The Penguin Historical Atlas of Ancient Civilizations
Author: John Haywood
Subject: Ancient History, Maps
Summary: Maps and commentary tracing the rise and spread of the ancient world's civilizations from Mesopotamia to Rome.

Title: The Pet Dragon: A Story about Adventure, Friendship, and Chinese Characters
Author: Christoph Niemann
Subject: Chinese Characters, Language, Friendship
Summary: A girl searches for her runaway pet dragon, and along the way each Chinese character is drawn into the illustration it names — teaching how the written characters grow out of pictures.

Title: The Pigeon Has Feelings, Too!
Author: Mo Willems
Subject: Emotions, Humor, Pigeon Series
Summary: The bus driver asks the Pigeon to look happy, and the Pigeon works through a run of other feelings instead. A board book entry in Willems's Pigeon series.

Title: The Pine Child
Author: Paul Edmund Thomas (art by Katie McCollow)
Subject: Winter, Forest, Wonder
Summary: A watercolor-illustrated winter tale from The Gabbro Head, following a small child through the snowy pinewoods toward the lamplight of a cabin.

Title: The Poetry of Science: The Poetry Friday Anthology for Science, For Kids
Author: compiled by Sylvia Vardell & Janet Wong (illustrated by Frank Ramspott & Bug Wang)
Subject: Science Poetry, STEM
Summary: 248 poems by 78 poets covering every area of science — matter, energy, life, earth and space — the student companion to the Poetry Friday Anthology for Science teacher edition.

Title: The Poppy War
Author: R.F. Kuang
Subject: Military Fantasy, China, Shamanism
Summary: A war orphan tests into an elite military academy and discovers a lethal shamanic power. Draws heavily on twentieth-century Chinese history.

Title: The Prince & the Coyote
Author: David Bowles (illustrated by Amanda Mijangos)
Subject: Aztec History, Nezahualcoyotl, Poetry
Summary: The story of Acolmiztli, the exiled prince who became the poet-king Nezahualcoyotl of Texcoco. A Pura Belpre-winning novel woven with translated Nahuatl verse.

Title: The Princess in the Forest
Author: Sibylle von Olfers
Subject: Fairies, Forest, Art Nouveau
Summary: A small princess wanders into the forest and is welcomed by its flower and animal children. One of von Olfers's early-twentieth-century nature fantasies in her distinctive decorative style.

Title: The Purloining of Prince Oleomargarine
Author: Mark Twain & Philip Stead (illustrated by Erin Stead)
Subject: Fairy Tales, Kindness
Summary: An unfinished Twain story completed a century later: a poor boy, magic seeds that let him talk to animals, and the search for a stolen prince.

Title: The Raccoon and the Bee Tree
Author: Charles Eastman & Elaine Goodale Eastman (illustrated by Jim Turnbull)
Subject: Dakota Culture, Folklore, Greed
Summary: A Dakota story of a greedy raccoon who takes more honey than he needs and pays for it, retold from the Eastmans' early-1900s collection.

Title: The Return of the Light: Twelve Tales from Around the World for the Winter Solstice
Author: Carolyn McVickar Edwards
Subject: Winter Solstice, World Folklore, Seasonal Celebration
Summary: Twelve solstice stories retold from North America, China, Scandinavia, India, Africa, South America, Europe, and Polynesia, with notes on the traditions behind them.

Title: The River Has Roots
Author: Amal El-Mohtar
Subject: Fairy Tale, Sisters, Folk Song
Summary: Two sisters tend the singing willows on the border between England and Faerie, until one of them is murdered. A novella built on the bones of the Twa Sisters ballad.

Title: The Roadmap to Literacy
Author: Janet Langley & Jennifer Militzer-Kopperl
Subject: Literacy Instruction, Waldorf Pedagogy
Summary: A comprehensive guide to teaching reading and writing in Waldorf grades 1–3, mapping the Renewal of Literacy approach onto phonics, spelling and language arts instruction.

Title: The Rock from the Sky
Author: Jon Klassen
Subject: Humor, Deadpan, Friendship
Summary: Five linked stories about a turtle, an armadillo, and a snake standing in spots of varying safety while something falls from above.

Title: The Romance of Tristan and Iseult
Author: Joseph Bedier
Subject: Arthurian Legend, Tragic Romance, Medieval
Summary: Bedier's reconstruction of the medieval Tristan legend from the surviving fragments. Slipcased edition.

Title: The Sagas of Icelanders
Author: Various (Penguin Classics Deluxe Edition)
Subject: Icelandic Sagas, Medieval Iceland, Norse
Summary: A selection of the medieval Icelandic family sagas and tales in modern translation, with maps, glossaries, and reference material.

Title: The School of Numbers
Author: Emily Hawkins (illustrated by Daniel Frost)
Subject: Mathematics
Summary: A space-academy-themed introduction to math for kids, teaching 40 short lessons — counting, shapes, measurement, fractions, symmetry, time and more — through cadets on missions with Professor Cosmo and friends.

Title: The Screwtape Letters
Author: C.S. Lewis
Subject: Christianity, Satire, Temptation
Summary: A senior devil writes to his nephew with advice on corrupting an ordinary man. Lewis's epistolary satire.

Title: The Secret Door
Author: Shelley Davidow
Subject: Phonics, Mystery, Adventure
Summary: Second chapter book in the phonetic reader series, mixing mystery and adventure with decoding practice in r-controlled vowels and vowel combinations (ar, or, er, ir, ur, oo, ou, ow, oi, oy, au, aw). Grades 2-4.

Title: The Secret Pet
Author: Shelley Davidow
Subject: Phonics, Friendship, Animals
Summary: First chapter book following the Early Reader Series: Tim befriends Jake the magical snake and smuggles him home and to school, and the two learn about the difference between life in the wild and life in a home, and how love changes our habits. Targets vowel teams, digraphs and open/closed syllables; grades 2-3.

Title: The Secret Wish
Author: Shelley Davidow
Subject: Phonics, Adventure
Summary: Final chapter book in the phonetic reader series, illustrated by Carol Liknaitzky, giving readers a story built around consonant blends and digraphs (qu, sh, th, wh, gl, pl, sl, gr, tr and others). Grades 3-4.

Title: The Seven-Year-Old Wonder Book
Author: Isabel Wyatt
Subject: Fairy Tales, Storytelling, Waldorf
Summary: Original stories written for the second-grade year in Waldorf schools, pitched at the change of consciousness around age seven.

Title: The Shadow of the Gods
Author: John Gwynne
Subject: Norse-Inspired, Gods, Vengeance
Summary: Three hundred years after the gods tore each other apart, their bones and bloodlines still shape the land. First of The Bloodsworn Saga.

Title: The Shadow of What Was Lost
Author: James Islington
Subject: Prophecy, Magic, Time
Summary: Twenty years after a rebellion stripped the Gifted of their powers, a young man discovers his own magic is different. First of the Licanius Trilogy.

Title: The Shortest Day: Celebrating the Winter Solstice
Author: Wendy Pfeffer (illustrated by Jesse Reisch)
Subject: Winter Solstice, Astronomy, World Traditions
Summary: Why the days shorten and lengthen, and how cultures around the world have marked the solstice, with activities and celebrations to try.

Title: The Shrouded Queen
Author: Ashley Tropea
Subject: Egyptian Mythology, Identity Swap, Trials
Summary: A slave and a princess trade places during an attack, sending each into a separate fight for survival. A romantasy debut drawing on ancient Egyptian mythology.

Title: The Song of Achilles
Author: Madeline Miller
Subject: Greek Mythology, Troy, Love Story
Summary: Patroclus narrates his life with Achilles from boyhood through the Trojan War. Winner of the Orange Prize.

Title: The Soul Would Have No Rainbow if the Eyes Had No Tears
Author: Guy A. Zona
Subject: Native American Proverbs, Wisdom
Summary: A gathering of Native American proverbs and sayings, arranged by theme.

Title: The Spellshop
Author: Sarah Beth Durst
Subject: Cozy Fantasy, Jam, Magic
Summary: A librarian flees a burning capital with the last of the spellbooks and opens a jam-and-spells shop on a remote island. Cozy fantasy.

Title: The Stoics Illustrated: Ancient Wisdom for Modern Living
Author: Paul Scade
Subject: Stoicism, Ancient Philosophy
Summary: An illustrated introduction to Stoic thought — Zeno, Seneca, Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius — and how their ideas on control, virtue and adversity apply to modern life.

Title: The Story Book of Science
Author: Jean-Henri Fabre
Subject: Natural History, Conversational Science, Classic
Summary: Uncle Paul answers children's questions about insects, plants, weather, and stones over the course of a year. A nineteenth-century classic widely used in living-books curricula.

Title: The Story of Amelia Earhart
Author: Adele de Leeuw (illustrated by Harry Beckhoff)
Subject: Amelia Earhart, Aviation, Signature Books
Summary: Earhart's life and record flights, written for young readers in the Signature Books series.

Title: The Story of Helen Keller
Author: Lorena A. Hickok (illustrated by Jo Polseno)
Subject: Helen Keller, Deafblindness, Signature Books
Summary: Helen Keller's life from the illness that took her sight and hearing through her work as a writer and advocate. Signature Books #45.

Title: The Story of Little Babaji
Author: Helen Bannerman (illustrated by Fred Marcellino)
Subject: Folktale, India, Tigers
Summary: A retitled and reillustrated version of the classic tale: a boy gives away his fine new clothes to tigers, who chase each other into butter for his pancakes.

Title: The Story of Little Billy Bluesocks
Author: Sibylle von Olfers
Subject: Fairies, Nature, Art Nouveau
Summary: Little Billy Bluesocks sets out from home and meets the creatures of the meadow and pond. Another of von Olfers's rounded, gently patterned picture books for the very young.

Title: The Story of Martha Washington
Author: Jeannette Covert Nolan (illustrated by Corinne B. Dillon)
Subject: Martha Washington, Colonial America, Signature Books
Summary: A biography of Martha Washington for young readers in the Grosset & Dunlap Signature Books series (#32).

Title: The Story of Rome for Kids: From the Legend of Romulus to the Fall of Caesar
Author: Tales of History
Subject: Ancient Rome, Republic, Narrative History
Summary: Roman history told as a story from the founding legend through the assassination of Caesar. No named author on the cover; credited to the Tales of History imprint.

Title: The Story of the Bible
Author: Charles Foster
Subject: Bible Stories, Old and New Testament, Vintage
Summary: Foster's nineteenth-century retelling of the Bible in simple language with several hundred illustrations. Antique illustrated binding.

Title: The Story of the Butterfly Children
Author: Sibylle von Olfers
Subject: Butterflies, Summer, Art Nouveau
Summary: The butterfly children live their summer among the flowers, hold a wedding, and weather a storm. Companion volume to the Root Children.

Title: The Story of the Declaration of Independence
Author: Norman Richards
Subject: American History, Founding Documents
Summary: A Cornerstones of Freedom account of how the Declaration was drafted, debated and signed.

Title: The Story of the Greeks
Author: H. A. Guerber
Subject: Ancient Greece, Classical History
Summary: A classic narrative history of ancient Greece for young readers, telling the story from the earliest settlers through Athens, Sparta, the Persian Wars and Alexander in short chapter-length episodes.

Title: The Story of the Orchestra
Author: Robert Levine (illustrated by Meredith Hamilton)
Subject: Orchestra, Composers, Classical Music
Summary: An introduction to the instruments of the orchestra and the composers who wrote for them, with a companion recording.

Title: The Story of the Roman Empire for Kids: From Augustus to the Fall of the Empire
Author: Tales of History
Subject: Roman Empire, Emperors, Narrative History
Summary: Picks up at Augustus and carries the story through the emperors to the fall of the western empire. No named author on the cover; credited to the Tales of History imprint.

Title: The Story of the Root Children
Author: Sibylle von Olfers
Subject: Seasons, Spring, Art Nouveau
Summary: Mother Earth wakes the root children in spring, they sew their bright clothes and go out into the world, and return underground in autumn. Von Olfers's best-known book and a staple of the Waldorf seasonal year.

Title: The Story of the Snow Children
Author: Sibylle von Olfers
Subject: Winter, Snow, Art Nouveau
Summary: Poppy is carried off by a snowflake to the winter queen's ice palace and returns home again. Von Olfers's winter counterpart to The Story of the Root Children.

Title: The Story of the World, Volume 1: Ancient Times
Author: Susan Wise Bauer
Subject: Ancient History, Homeschool Curriculum, Narrative History
Summary: World history told as a sequence of stories from the earliest nomads to the fall of Rome. The first of four volumes in a widely used classical homeschool history.

Title: The Story of Ulysses S. Grant
Author: Jeannette Covert Nolan (illustrated by Lynd Ward)
Subject: Ulysses S. Grant, Civil War, Signature Books
Summary: Grant's life from Ohio boyhood through the Civil War and the presidency. Signature Books #6, illustrated by Lynd Ward.

Title: The Story-Book of Science
Author: Jean-Henri Fabre
Subject: Natural History, Insects, Science
Summary: The French entomologist teaches natural science through evening conversations between Uncle Paul and the children, covering insects, plants, weather, minerals and the workings of the natural world in story form.

Title: The Sun Egg
Author: Elsa Beskow
Subject: Forest Fairies, Oranges, Swedish Classic
Summary: A woodland fairy finds an orange in the forest and is certain it is a fallen piece of the sun, until a visiting bird explains what it really is. Another of Beskow's early-twentieth-century Swedish nature stories.

Title: The Tales of Tiptoes Lightly
Author: Reg Down
Subject: Nature Stories, Fairies, Seasons
Summary: Three gentle nature tales — The Bee Who Lost His Buzz, Pumpkin Crow, and Lucy Goose and the Half-Egg — starring the fairy Tiptoes Lightly and her woodland friends.

Title: The Testaments
Author: Margaret Atwood
Subject: Gilead, Testimony, Resistance
Summary: Three narrators, including Aunt Lydia, testify to the inner workings and unravelling of Gilead. Atwood's Booker-winning sequel to The Handmaid's Tale.

Title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
Author: Mac Barnett (illustrated by Jon Klassen)
Subject: Folktales, Trolls, Humor
Summary: A deadpan retelling of the Norwegian folktale, with three goats, one bridge, and a troll who gets exactly what he deserves.

Title: The Three Questions
Author: Jon J Muth
Subject: Ethics, Zen Buddhism, Kindness
Summary: Based on Tolstoy's story: a boy asks when is the best time, who is most important, and what is the right thing to do, and finds the answers by helping someone in need.

Title: The Untethered Soul Guided Journal
Author: Michael A. Singer
Subject: Reflection, Prompts, Spirituality
Summary: A prompted journal companion to The Untethered Soul, with space for written reflection on each theme.

Title: The Untethered Soul: The Journey Beyond Yourself
Author: Michael A. Singer
Subject: Consciousness, Meditation, Letting Go
Summary: Singer on the inner voice, the habit of clinging to thought and emotion, and what it means to stop identifying with either.

Title: The Upper Case: Trouble in Capital City
Author: Tara Lazar (illustrated by Ross MacDonald)
Subject: Grammar, Capitalization, Mystery
Summary: Private eye Question Mark investigates a case of missing capital letters in a punctuation-themed detective caper.

Title: The Usborne Internet-Linked Encyclopedia of World History
Author: Usborne
Subject: World History
Summary: A illustrated survey of world history from prehistory to the modern era, with recommended web links for each topic.

Title: The Very Last Leaf
Author: Stef Wade
Subject: Autumn, Anxiety, Courage
Summary: Lance the leaf is top of his class but terrified of falling, in a story about performance anxiety and letting go.

Title: The Very Short, Entirely True History of Unicorns
Author: Sarah Laskow (illustrated by Sam Beck)
Subject: Unicorns, Myth vs. Fact, Natural History
Summary: Traces where unicorn legends actually came from -- misread travelogues, narwhal tusks, mistranslated scripture -- and how the beast changed shape over two thousand years.

Title: The Voyages of Christopher Columbus
Author: Armstrong Sperry
Subject: Exploration, Atlantic Crossing, Landmark Books
Summary: Columbus's four voyages recounted for young readers in the Landmark Books series.

Title: The Waldorf Book of Poetry
Author: David Kennedy
Subject: Poetry, Verse, Waldorf Pedagogy
Summary: A large collection of poems gathered for Waldorf classrooms and homes, organized for recitation across the grades and the seasons.

Title: The Way of Gnome (Tales of Limindoor Woods, Book 1)
Author: Sieglinde De Francesca
Subject: Gnomes, Nature Stories, Waldorf
Summary: A prequel to A Donsy of Gnomes in which young Gus learns the 'Way of Gnome' — a code of kindness, generosity and courage — while readers discover how the gnomes first came to the magic forest of Limindoor and found their Gifts. Gentle read-aloud chapter book for ages 6+.

Title: The Way of Kings
Author: Brandon Sanderson
Subject: Roshar, Storms, Knights Radiant
Summary: On a world scoured by highstorms, a slave, a scholar, and a highprince circle the return of an ancient order. First of The Stormlight Archive.

Title: The Wild Robot
Author: Peter Brown
Subject: Robots, Island, Nature
Summary: A robot washes ashore on a wild island and slowly learns the language and rules of the animals living there. First of the Wild Robot trilogy.

Title: The Will of the Many
Author: James Islington
Subject: Roman Empire, Hierarchy, Academy
Summary: In an empire where citizens cede their will up the hierarchy, an exiled prince hides in plain sight at its most prestigious academy. First of the Hierarchy series.

Title: The Wise Enchanter: A Journey Through the Alphabet
Author: Shelley Davidow (illustrated by Krystyna E. Kurzyca)
Subject: Alphabet, Fantasy, Language
Summary: A quest story in which children journey through the alphabet, each letter unlocking part of an enchanted adventure.

Title: The Wonder of Lullabies
Author: Mary Thienes-Schunemann
Subject: Lullabies, Singing with Children, Waldorf
Summary: Lullabies gathered from around the world with guitar chords and a companion CD, meant for singing with children of any age. Revised edition in the Singing with Children series; a Naturally You Can Sing production.

Title: The Wonders of Nature
Author: DK
Subject: Nature, Natural History
Summary: A gilt-edged illustrated compendium of the natural world's most extraordinary plants, animals, minerals and phenomena.

Title: The Wondrous Workings of Planet Earth
Author: Rachel Ignotofsky
Subject: Ecology, Ecosystems, Earth Science
Summary: Illustrated infographics explaining ecosystems, biomes and the cycles that keep the planet running.

Title: The World of the Old Testament: A Curious Kid's Guide to the Bible's Most Ancient Stories
Author: Marc Olson (illustrated by Jemima Maybank)
Subject: Bible History, Ancient Near East
Summary: Infographics, maps and charts explaining who the people of the Old Testament were — what they ate, how they worked, fought and worshipped — and how that context changes how the stories read.

Title: Therapeutic Storytelling: 101 Healing Stories for Children
Author: Susan Perrow
Subject: Storytelling, Child Behavior, Healing
Summary: A collection of metaphorical stories written to address specific childhood challenges — fear, grief, anger, bedwetting, bullying — plus guidance on writing your own healing stories.

Title: They Both Die at the End
Author: Adam Silvera
Subject: Mortality, Friendship, One Day
Summary: Two strangers get the call telling them they will die today, and spend their last day together. A New York-set novel about living fully in one day.

Title: Thirteen Moons on Turtle's Back
Author: Joseph Bruchac & Jonathan London (illustrated by Thomas Locker)
Subject: Native American Legends, Seasons
Summary: Thirteen poems, one for each moon of the year, drawn from the legends of different Native nations and painted in luminous landscapes.

Title: This Is Monet
Author: Sara Pappworth (illustrated by Aude Van Ryn)
Subject: Monet, Impressionism
Summary: A pocket-sized illustrated life of Claude Monet, tracing his career and the making of Impressionism.

Title: This Is Not My Hat
Author: Jon Klassen
Subject: Humor, Deadpan, Fish
Summary: A small fish steals a hat from a much bigger fish and explains, confidently, why he'll get away with it. Winner of the Caldecott Medal; board book edition.

Title: This Is the Way We Wash-a-Day
Author: Mary Thienes-Schunemann (illustrated by Lura Schwarz-Smith)
Subject: Work Songs, Daily Rhythm, Waldorf
Summary: Songs for the ordinary work of the day -- washing, gardening, tidying -- with guitar chords, a CD, and an interview with Pete Seeger. Part of the Singing with Children series.

Title: This Kingdom Will Not Kill Me
Author: Ilona Andrews
Subject: Portal Fantasy, Immortality, Court Intrigue
Summary: Maggie wakes in the brutal world of her favorite unfinished fantasy series and discovers she cannot die -- though everyone she comes to love can. First of the Maggie the Undying trilogy.

Title: This Song Is (Not) for You
Author: Laura Nowlin
Subject: Music, Friendship, Polyamory
Summary: Three friends in a band navigate love that doesn't fit the shape they expected. A YA novel about asexuality and chosen relationships.

Title: Three Grimms' Fairy Tales
Author: Brothers Grimm (paintings by Gerard Wagner)
Subject: Fairy Tales, Anthroposophical Art
Summary: Three Grimm tales paired with the color paintings of anthroposophical artist Gerard Wagner.

Title: Through Your Eyes: My Child's Gift to Me
Author: Ainsley Earhardt (illustrated by Ji-Hyuk Kim)
Subject: Mother and Child, Wonder, Everyday Moments
Summary: A mother sets out to show her daughter the world and finds her daughter showing it back to her, in the small things she would have hurried past. Told in verse with soft, impressionistic paintings.

Title: To the Edge of the Universe
Author: Raman Prinja (illustrated by John Hersey)
Subject: Astronomy, Cosmology
Summary: A fold-out journey outward from Earth to the observable edge of the universe, scaled step by step.

Title: Today I Will Fly!
Author: Mo Willems
Subject: Perseverance, Friendship
Summary: Piggie is determined to fly and Gerald is sure it is impossible — until a little help from a passing bird proves him wrong.

Title: Tomo-chan Is a Girl! Vol. 1-3
